correctness.rationale: In the fixed-root out-tree each downstream vertex contributes exactly p^depth to expected occupation. Closing its gateway removes that contribution, and no other branch is affected. A feasible branch profile starts with 1 and the remaining widths form an arbitrary positive composition of its remaining size; assigning every vertex at each level a parent in the preceding level realizes every profile, including the singleton with empty composition. Every admissible tree is therefore represented by a pair of profiles whose sizes sum to n−1; identical profiles give a tie. The fractional-linear map p=t/(1+t) sends the open unit interval bijectively to the positive half-line and clearing denominators gives the stated integer coefficients; Descartes' bound applies after ignoring zeros. Independently, I enumerated compositions by cut combinations, visited unequal-sized profile pairs once and equally sized pairs by combinations, removed endpoint factors and counted distinct roots by exact Sturm sequences. Across orders 3–13, 3056 distinct profile pairs were checked and none had more than one interior root. Orders below 3 cannot support two gateways. At 14 the listed graph has profiles (1,1,4) and (1,2,1,1,2). Their benefit difference factors as −p²(2p−1)(p²+p−1), with exactly two simple interior roots and signs negative, positive, negative. The preferred closure is indeed the one with greater benefit.
residual_risks: The exhaustive lower-order check concerns profiles, not individual labeled trees. Completeness rests on the exact profile reduction. Neither a classification of all order-14 witnesses nor a calibrated containment forecast was checked or asserted.

evidence: Frozen proof identifies the comparison as a difference of two rooted level polynomials, with one factor of p from entering the respective branches.

For adjacent candidate endpoints on an undirected tree, cutting their common edge gives rooted components with rooted expected-size polynomials H_A,H_B. Their source-size difference is (1−p)(H_A−H_B). Thus two-switch minima in this equivalent adjacent-endpoint problem would be at order 13, one less than the gateway problem. The inspected source-ranking result proves one switch first at seven and checks only orders through seven.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The positive factors p and 1−p cannot alter interior crossings. An adjacent-source two-switch census would therefore be material prior coverage. The compared result does not perform that census, and the targeted equivalent-formulation lookup supplied only different statistics or graph families.

value.rationale: Rooted reliability rankings and parameter-dependent edge importance are independently motivated by prior network-reliability work. The fixed-root, two-gateway restriction isolates whether ranking can return to its initial order with a single varying probability even when site values and intervention costs are identical. The exact 14-site boundary and explicit strict preference intervals answer that question more sharply than an isolated reversal or example without minimality.
residual_risks: This is a mathematical boundary for an abstract model, not empirical support for applying its thresholds to real networks.
